title: Humayun Enters Bengal and Occupies Gaur
subtitle: The first major Mughal intervention phase reaches Bengal's political core.
summary: In 1538, Humayun's campaign reached Bengal and occupied Gaur, signaling the first major Mughal intervention into Bengal's power structure. Although temporary, the move tied Bengal directly to the Mughal-Afghan contest in the east.
heroTagline: Humayun's Bengal push opened a new imperial contest over the region.
whyItMatters: This event matters because it marks the beginning of sustained Mughal strategic engagement with Bengal, even before durable provincial control was possible.
longTermLegacy: The 1538 campaign established Bengal as a central theater in Mughal eastern policy, setting up later rounds of conquest, reversal, and re-entry.
identityMemoryNotes: In historical memory, 1538 represents the opening of the Mughal-Afghan struggle that would shape Bengal's sixteenth-century transition.

claimCitations.claim: In 1538, Humayun's campaign reached Bengal and occupied Gaur, signaling the first major Mughal intervention into Bengal's power structure. Although temporary, the move tied Bengal directly to the Mughal-Afghan contest in the east.
This event matters because it marks the beginning of sustained Mughal strategic engagement with Bengal, even before durable provincial control was possible.
The 1538 campaign established Bengal as a central theater in Mughal eastern policy, setting up later rounds of conquest, reversal, and re-entry.
In historical memory, 1538 represents the opening of the Mughal-Afghan struggle that would shape Bengal's sixteenth-century transition.
